narrative.overview: The reptile-keeping app Apple could have shipped: iOS conventions played straight, at Things 3's level of finish, with the keeper's evening round as the only content. Calm and grey by default, colour spent only on what needs doing, light and dark from the phone.
keyCharacteristics: iOS system conventions at full fidelity; no custom chrome.
Light and dark from the phone, with Apple's increased-contrast variants where needed for AA.
One tint, system green, for what can be tapped and what is going well.
Red and orange only for an animal or task that needs something.
Inset grouped lists and summary tiles as the containers.
SF Pro on Apple's text styles; 11pt floor.

rules.name: The Earned Colour Rule
rules.body: Red and orange mean an animal or a task needs something; never a cost, category or decoration.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: Green marks what can be tapped and what is going well; anything else is a label grey.

rules.name: The Eleven Point Floor
rules.body: Nothing outside the tab bar is set below 11px.

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Counts, weights, money and days use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Flat Cell Rule
rules.body: A list section or tile never casts a shadow or carries a border.

dos: Do use the semantic tokens so both appearances follow.
Do build screens from large title, grouped list sections and summary tiles.
Do keep figures tabular and on the type ramp.
Do give every motion a fade-only path under Reduce Motion, and animate transform and opacity only.
Do use the named springs and curves rather than new ones.
Do show loading, failed and empty as three different states.
donts: Don't put a border or shadow on a list section, tile or card.
Don't carry status in a coloured stripe down a row's edge.
Don't use red or orange for anything that does not need doing.
Don't load a web font or add a second accent hue.
